headline: High: shared project-directory writes and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; TREK’s MCP/browser surface amplifies the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a shared project directory and TREK can use MCP plus browser/web inputs, so content from one can be consumed by the other through files or shared workflows. This is not proven as a default direct bridge, but the interaction is plausible and the shared directory makes instruction-hijack risk real.
conditions: IF TREK reads prompts or task text from files written by gpt-engineer, injected instructions can propagate.
IF either agent treats shared project files as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Disable automatic ingestion of file contents as instructions.
Add a human review step before TREK acts on generated text.
Use provenance labels on files exchanged between agents.
requires-engineering: add sandboxed, read-only handoff files with schema validation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer has broad network egress and handles OPENAI_API_KEY, while TREK touches reservations, API keys, MFA secrets, and logs to local files. If they share a project directory or operator workflow, sensitive travel data can be exposed to gpt-engineer’s model calls or outputs can leak into TREK’s collaborative surfaces.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory, generated code or logs may expose travel secrets.
IF gpt-engineer sends file contents to a third-party model, TREK data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep TREK secrets out of the gpt-engineer workspace.
Redact API keys and MFA secrets before any handoff.
Restrict gpt-engineer to non-sensitive sample data.
Review outbound requests from gpt-engineer before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret isolation and egress allowlists.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer can write the project filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and TREK is a real-time collaborative app with shared mutable files and WebSocket/MCP surfaces. Even without explicit git writes, overlapping writes to the same workspace can race and corrupt code or data.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project directory, file races can overwrite each other’s changes.
IF TREK persists collaborative state while gpt-engineer rewrites files, inconsistent state can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock.
Pause TREK edits while gpt-engineer runs.
Back up the workspace before each run.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer produces code and files that TREK can plausibly ingest through collaborative or MCP-enabled workflows. TREK’s real-time, action-oriented surfaces mean unverified generated artifacts can cascade into incorrect plans, reservations, or user-visible outputs. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF TREK consumes gpt-engineer output without review, incorrect code or text can propagate downstream.
IF generated artifacts are used as authoritative inputs, errors can affect reservations or user-facing actions.
mitigations: Require manual review of all generated artifacts.
Mark gpt-engineer output as untrusted by default.
Use a checklist before TREK acts on imported content.
Limit imported content to non-actionable drafts.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles sensitive travel and identity data, including API keys, MFA secrets, reservations, and country visit history. gpt-engineer has broad egress and can send file contents to a configured model, so if TREK data enters its workspace, compliance exposure can occur without a residency or retention control shown in either profile.
conditions: IF TREK data includes EU PII or secrets and is processed by gpt-engineer, residency and retention obligations may be breached.
IF logs or prompts retain reservation or identity data, subject-rights handling may be impaired.
mitigations: Exclude regulated travel data from gpt-engineer prompts.
Minimize logging of secrets and identifiers.
Confirm data residency before sharing any TREK content.
Delete temporary handoff files after use.
requires-engineering: implement retention and residency controls per data class.
